payload.claim: Change the view constructively if: (a) Mercedes-Benz Cars adjusted Return on Sales guidance is raised above the current 3–5% band for FY2027 and China retail volumes stop declining YoY for two consecutive quarters; (b) the company discloses an industrial-only leverage figure showing industrial net debt/EBITDA materially below the 5.2x group number; (c) the dividend is reset to a payout that the trough earnings actually cover, removing the distress signal. Change the view negatively if: industrial FCF guidance falls below €3bn, further China impairments recur in a second consecutive quarter, the 40-model offensive slips beyond 2027, or the conduct gate escalates from Flag toward evidence that fines are a price of the business model rather than legacy items.

prediction.reasoning: Company guidance itself caps Cars adjusted RoS at 3–5% with revenue slightly below prior year and industrial FCF below €5.4bn, and the TTM EBIT margin has been flat-to-down (4.69% → 4.78%) even with a Q2 beat; reaching 6.0% on rolling twelve months by mid-2027 would require ~24% EBIT growth on falling revenue. This differs from the sell-side recovery path embedded in the ~9x forward P/E and the €57.2 target, while still rejecting the price's implied halving of steady-state earnings.
